newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel increases size of Leumi issue.
newsitem.headline: Israel increases size of Leumi issue.

text.p: The Israeli government will increase the size of a Bank Leumi public offering to $150 million in shares and warrants from $125 million, one of the underwriters said on Tuesday.
This follows the success of the first part of the offering -- involving pre-commitments from institutional investors -- which closed on Monday, the IBI investment house said.
Some 20 European institutional investors pre-commmitted to purchasing $120 million worth of shares and warrants.
A further $30 million worth will be sold in the offering open to the general public, on May 27.
The government originally planned to sell $100 million overseas and $25 million in Israel.
The institutional investors committed to the minimum price of five shekels a share, which will be set in the prospectus to be published on Wednesday.
Bank Leumi shares traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange closed at 5.41 shekels on Monday.
The Israeli government will raise another $150 million if all the warrants are exercised -- some in six months and the rest in a year, IBI said.
The shares and warrants together represent 12 percent of Leumi, Israel's second largest bank.
The government owns 82 percent of Leumi shares with the remainder already in public hands.
The government expects to raise three billion shekels from the sale of Israeli bank shares this year.
